title.value: Adaptive Learning of Tensor Network Structures
title.justification: The paper is primarily centered around developing a new algorithm for learning tensor network structures, as indicated by its title and numerous references throughout the document.
title.quote: Tensor Networks (TN) offer a powerful framework to efficiently represent very high-dimensional objects... In this work, we leverage the TN formalism to develop a generic and efficient adaptive algorithm to jointly learn the structure and the parameters of a TN from data.

extractions.description: The paper discusses the development of a generic and efficient adaptive algorithm to learn the structure and parameters of a Tensor Network (TN). The method utilizes a greedy approach to iteratively build tensor network structures by identifying promising edges for rank increments. Experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness in tensor decomposition, completion, and model compression tasks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on developing algorithms for tensor network learning, which is a fundamental machine learning problem. There is no mention of direct applications or discussions related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Tensor Networks (TN) offer a powerful framework to efficiently represent very high-dimensional objects. TN have recently shown their potential for machine learning applications... Our method is based on a simple greedy approach starting from a rank one tensor...

primary_category.quote: In particular, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art evolutionary topology search introduced in [18] for tensor decomposition of images (while being orders of magnitude faster) and finds efficient structures to compress neural networks outperforming popular TT based approaches.

new_primary_category.quote: Akin to matrix factorization, tensor methods rely on factorizing a high-order tensor into small factors. However, in contrast with matrices, there are many different ways of decomposing a tensor, each one giving rise to a different notion of rank.
